cases.answer: In Jan et al. (Pakistani/Pashtun T2DM patients on sulphonylureas), the CYP2C9*2 allele frequency was 17.5% in hypoglycaemia cases (35 alleles) vs 6.0% in controls (12). At genotype level, *1/*2 was 10% (n=20) in cases vs 6.0% (n=12) in controls, and *2/*2 was 7% vs 3.5% (n=7 in controls). Combined *2 carriage by genotype is therefore about 17% of cases vs 9.5% of controls. Note the table prints n=20 for *2/*2 cases but 7%.

cases.answer: The review does not describe a distinction framed as acute adaptive HIF-1α activation versus chronic overactivation. It distinguishes acute hypoxia (adaptation through sodium ions as second messengers affecting mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation) from prolonged chronic hypoxia (mainly regulated by HIF-1). It presents HIF-1α as having mainly protective roles in DKD. I found no passage about chronic overactivation of HIF-1α being harmful.

cases.answer: Djoumessi et al. (17 patients with resistant hypertension and T2DM in Cameroon) reported that low-dose 25 mg spironolactone reduced office systolic BP by 33 mmHg vs 14 mmHg with the alternative treatment (p=0.024). Office diastolic BP fell by 14 vs 5 mmHg (p=0.006). Follow-up was 4 weeks, with visits at baseline, 2 weeks and 4 weeks. This is not a fourth-line label in the passages read.

cases.answer: The sleep review (Ghanem et al.) cites Isomaa et al. as a cohort of 4483 subjects aged 35–70. It reports that metabolic syndrome raised cardiovascular risk (RRs of 2.96 for CAD, 2.63 for MI and 2.27 for stroke), so it is prospective evidence of outcomes. Mbota et al. is a hospital-based cross-sectional study of 139 T2DM patients in Buea that estimates prevalence of metabolic syndrome (64.00% by IDF and 56.80% by NCEP ATP criteria). It looks at its association with glycemic control, not outcomes.

cases.answer: The twelve-month HbA1c difference is not reported. The Berthoumieux et al. randomized trial in the articles lasted 6 months. HbA1c was lower with digital DSMES+CGM than usual care at 3 months (−0.7%, P=.03) and at 6 months (−0.6%, 95% CI −1.4% to 0.2%, P=.12, not significant). A separate 'long-term results' Berthoumieux paper is only a reference-list entry, with no results.
